title: QBR - Crestline Health Check
summary: Quarterly business review focused on usage trends, cost drivers, reliability incidents, and roadmap alignment. Customer interested in Dedicated sizing, P95/P99 latency improvements, and security docs for upcoming procurement review.
next_steps: Maya to send updated pricing and Dedicated sizing options by 2026-07-05
Sofia to schedule benchmark run for P95/P99 on dedicated pool w/ Crestline sample traffic by 2026-07-09
Liam to share QBR slide deck and usage report link
Priya to confirm procurement timeline and required security artifacts
action_items: Sofia: Run P95/P99 benchmark and share logs (due 2026-07-09)
Liam: Upload QBR deck and usage CSV to shared folder (due 2026-07-02)
Priya: Confirm procurement timeline and list of compliance docs needed (no date given)
Evan: Provide representative prompt set and traffic profile for benchmark (due 2026-07-06)
header: Date: 2026-07-01 | Time: 10:00 - 11:00 PDT | Duration: 60m | Location: Zoom | Recording: yes
transcript: 00:00:05 Maya Chen: Alright everyone we can get started. Thanks for joining the QBR, appreciate you all making time.
00:00:13 Evan Brooks: Yeah thanks Maya, uh Priya and I will run through the usage and then jump into cost questions, Mark's on for the procurement bits.
00:00:22 Maya Chen: Perfect, quick round robin — me and Liam from CS, Sofia from SE, and on your side?
00:00:29 Priya Kapoor: Priya here, Platform Engineering. Evan's Head of ML, Mark's the CIO as Evan said.
00:00:36 Liam Patel: Cool, agenda — usage trends, cost drivers, reliability incidents last quarter, Dedicated options, roadmap alignment, and next steps.

00:00:48 Evan Brooks: Sounds good, let's jump in. Our main thing has been growth in embedding usage, about 2.4x since last quarter, and generation traffic steady except spikes around product launches.
00:01:05 Maya Chen: Nice — do you have the breakdown by route/model? Embeddings vs chat vs completion?

00:01:12 Evan Brooks: Yeah, embeddings are 57% of token volume, chat is 30%, completion 13%. Most embeddings use the open-small models, but we've started moving some to the verified medium for quality reasons.
00:01:28 Sofia Ramos: Are you using batching and caching on your embedding ingestion pipeline? I recall in the onboarding we suggested prefix caching for repeated queries.
00:01:35 Priya Kapoor: We enabled server-side batching but didn't fully configure the prefix cache; that was deferred to avoid risk during launch.

00:01:44 Liam Patel: That aligns with one of the cost drivers — lack of cache + small batch sizes increases per-token unit cost. We can recommend batching thresholds and cache TTLs that usually lower cost 20-40%.
00:01:58 Evan Brooks: That would help, yes. We also noticed tail latency spikes — P95 is fine but P99s jump during peak. That's been a blocker for some user flows.

00:02:08 Sofia Ramos: On the tail latency, two levers — Dedicated capacity with pinned workers reduces queuing, and the runtime's aggressive prefetch/batch policies can help. We should run a dedicated benchmark with your traffic profile.
00:02:20 Priya Kapoor: Can you clarify what "Dedicated" buys us compared to hosted? I know about reserved GPUs but need specifics for SLA and isolation.

00:02:28 Maya Chen: Sure — Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools reserved for your account, predictable throughput with commit sizing, optional burst capacity, and SLA-backed uptime/latency. For compliance, data stays logically separated and logs can be forwarded to your SIEM.
00:02:44 Mark Delaney: On compliance — we have an upcoming procurement review. We'll need SOC 2 docs, encryption details, and KMS integration notes. Can you send the artifacts?

00:02:54 Liam Patel: Absolutely — I'll share the security pack after the call. It includes SOC 2 report, KMS/HSM integration guide, and SSO/SAML setup notes. We'll also add an architecture diagram for VPC peering.
00:03:06 Mark Delaney: Great, that helps speed procurement. Timeline likely mid-July for procurement decision.
00:03:12 Evan Brooks: Back to performance, any quick wins we can do before Dedicated? Like tuning batching or quantization?

00:03:18 Sofia Ramos: For sure. On existing hosted setup you can enable larger batch sizes for background ingestion, enable prefix KV caching for repeated prompts, and consider moving some inference to quantized model variants for lower cost with acceptable quality drop.
00:03:32 Priya Kapoor: How risky is quantization for our production prompts? We can't degrade retrieval quality too much.

00:03:38 Sofia Ramos: It depends on model and whether it's embeddings or generation. For embeddings, int8 quant tends to be low risk. We'll recommend a candidate model and run an eval on your prompt set first.
00:03:48 Evan Brooks: Ok let's add that to the benchmark scope.
00:03:52 Maya Chen: I'll note that — benchmark to include P95/P99 latency, cost per 1M embeddings, and quality delta for quantized embeddings on your eval prompts.

00:03:59 Liam Patel: On cost — your monthly invoice increased 38% YoY mostly from embeddings. If we enable caching + batching and move warm traffic to a Dedicated pool, you should see meaningful savings.
00:04:12 Priya Kapoor: Can you give ballpark numbers for Dedicated vs Hosted cost per token? We need to justify to finance.

00:04:19 Maya Chen: Ballpark is tricky without sizing, but customers with heavy, predictable embedding workloads often see 20-45% unit cost reduction after Dedicated plus batch/cache optimizations. We'll send a tailored TCO with sizing options.
00:04:31 Evan Brooks: One more reliability note — we had two incidents last quarter where KV cache warmed incorrectly after a deploy. It caused a 5-10% error rate spike for ~20 minutes.

00:04:41 Sofia Ramos: Thanks for flagging that. We can look at rollout policies — canary with automatic fallback and model variant pinning. Also instrument tracing so we can fast-fallback on cache misses.
00:04:53 Priya Kapoor: Is model pinning available on Hosted? We want to avoid surprises during upgrades.
00:04:58 Maya Chen: Yes, model pinning and rollout controls are available across hosted and Dedicated. For private deployments there are additional controls too.
00:05:06 Mark Delaney: Are there any upcoming Redwood roadmap items we should care about? Async batching changes or new cost tooling?

00:05:12 Sofia Ramos: We're rolling out Redwood Optimize suggestions in the console — automated batching and cache recommendations with expected savings estimates. Also improved P99 tracing in the next quarter.
00:05:22 Evan Brooks: That Optimize feature could be useful — can we get early access?
00:05:25 Maya Chen: We can add you to the pilot program; I'll confirm with product after the call.
00:05:31 Liam Patel: Quick recap of agreed actions — we run benchmarks, share pricing, send security artifacts, and scope quantization evals. Anything else?
00:05:40 Priya Kapoor: We'll provide the prompt set and traffic sample within a week.
00:05:44 Maya Chen: Perfect. Sofia, will you lead the benchmark and include quantization and Dedicated sizing?
00:05:50 Sofia Ramos: Yep, I'll coordinate with Priya and Evan on inputs, run the P95/P99 tests, and share results + logs.
00:05:57 Evan Brooks: Do you expect any downtime for benchmarks? We need to schedule during low traffic windows.
00:06:03 Sofia Ramos: Benchmarks won't impact your production — we'll run against a dedicated test pool or a mirrored traffic stream. We'll coordinate the window with Priya.
00:06:11 Mark Delaney: For procurement, we'll want a formal quote for Dedicated options and an SLA addendum. Please send both.
00:06:18 Maya Chen: We'll put together 3 sizing tiers with corresponding commit levels and estimated savings. Quote and SLA addendum by 2026-07-05.
00:06:25 Liam Patel: I'll also upload the QBR slides and the usage CSV to the shared folder after this call.
00:06:31 Priya Kapoor: One last question — data residency. Some EU users' data needs to stay in EU regions. Are you able to scope region pins?
00:06:39 Maya Chen: Yes, region pinning is supported for Hosted and Dedicated — we can route EU traffic to EU regions and provide audit logs for residency verification.
00:06:47 Evan Brooks: Ok great. That covers my list.
00:06:50 Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts and the benchmark plan. Any final comments?
00:06:56 Mark Delaney: No, sounds good. Thanks.
00:07:00 Liam Patel: Thanks all — action items captured.
00:07:05 Maya Chen: Meeting adjourned.
